instructions:
You are building in the person's own open theprototype.app tab: a live, shared 3D scene. Every change shows for everyone in the session and can be undone.
This may be a VOICE conversation: answer in one or two short spoken sentences and say what changed in plain words ("Added three trees by the fire"). Never read out uuids, lists of numbers or JSON.
If a tool says the tab is closed or not connected, tell the person to open theprototype.app and press Connect Claude, then wait; do not retry in a loop.
Call status first: it says whether you may edit (a viewer can only look).
When the person says "undo that" or "take that back", call undo_last; if it refuses, say who changed what.
You act as this person in their own tab: status "you" is them (their peer id, name and role); the other users are everyone else.
Call list_scene before editing so you use real uuids; batch many objects into one call.
For "in front of me", call where_are_users and build at the spots it gives, facing the person (face_user: true). For "here" or "this", build at the person's latest ping: at: {ping: "latest"}; ask them to ping (Ctrl+Alt+click, or Ping in the menu) if they have none.
Motion and interaction are flow nodes (create_flow_nodes); call describe_node_types before wiring edges.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.
When asked what you can do here, call what_can_you_do and say its "say" line.

tools.name: list_scene
tools.title: Read the scene
tools.description:
List every object currently in the scene with its uuid, name, type, parent, transform, material, color and (for a primitive) its shape — geometry {type, sizes such as the thickness of a wall}. Every mesh also has mesh {vertexCount, faceCount (triangles), bounds {local, world}} — each box [[minX, minY, minZ], [maxX, maxY, maxZ]], local in the mesh's own space (its vertices), world in the scene. The transform is the AUTHORED pose: an object an effect is moving also has animated: true, and live {position, rotation, scale, visible} when this frame differs; update_objects writes the authored pose, so never copy live back into it. Call this before editing so you use real uuids. On a big scene narrow it: brief (uuids + names only), name (a glob), type, near {position, radius}. A big flow graph shows its first page and says how to read the rest: pass {flow: "scene" | object uuid, page} to read one page of one graph.
If a tool says the tab is closed or not connected, tell the person to open theprototype.app and press Connect Claude, then wait; do not retry in a loop.
Call list_scene before editing so you use real uuids; batch many objects into one call.

tools.name: create_objects
tools.title: Add objects
tools.description:
Create one or more primitives, lights or empty groups in a single call. Ground is the y=0 plane; place objects so they rest ON it (a box of height h sits at y=h/2). Returns the new uuids. To copy an existing object instead (a row of fence posts, a ring of chairs), pass from: its uuid, count, offset [x,y,z] between one copy and the next, and optionally randomRot / randomScale with a seed: deep copies (children, materials, flows), one undo step, uuids in order, in the source's own group. lookAt turns an object so its local +Z axis (its front) faces a point or another object, +Y kept up.
This may be a VOICE conversation: answer in one or two short spoken sentences and say what changed in plain words ("Added three trees by the fire"). Never read out uuids, lists of numbers or JSON.
Call list_scene before editing so you use real uuids; batch many objects into one call.
For "in front of me", call where_are_users and build at the spots it gives, facing the person (face_user: true). For "here" or "this", build at the person's latest ping: at: {ping: "latest"}; ask them to ping (Ctrl+Alt+click, or Ping in the menu) if they have none.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: animate_parts
tools.title: Animate parts
tools.description:
Animate a model's NAMED PARTS (child nodes from list_scene: a rotor, a door, a lid) with one clip — e.g. spin a rotor: tracks [{part: 'rotor', keys: [{t: 0, rot: [0, 0, 0]}, {t: 1, rot: [0, 360, 0]}]}], loop true. Keys are offsets from each part's rest pose (mode 'relative', the default; 'absolute' = local values). rot is Euler degrees [x, y, z]; pos metres [x, y, z]; scale a factor. The clip is saved as a .tpanim file, plays on every peer, and is one undo step.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: set_geometry
tools.title: Reshape objects
tools.description:
Reshape existing objects in place (they keep uuid, transform, material and flows): change a primitive's params (the keys list_scene shows under geometry, e.g. {width, height, depth} for a Box, {radiusTop, radiusBottom, height, radialSegments} for a Cylinder, {segments, phiLength} for a Lathe, {depth, bevel} for an extrusion), or its TYPE (box → Cylinder) with params on top of the new type's defaults. A tube (create_tube) takes path, radius / radii, closed. An object whose vertices were hand-edited refuses unless force: true (the rebuild replaces those edits). Up to 100 objects per call, one undo step.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

Editable afterwards with set_geometry (segments, phiLength). Returns the uuid.

tools.title: Extrude an outline

Editable with set_geometry (depth, bevel …). Returns the uuid.

tools.name: edit_mesh
tools.title: Edit a mesh
tools.description:
Model an existing mesh like Edit Mesh does: run ops on a selection of its faces or vertices. Face ops: extrude {distance}, inset {amount 0-1}, move {distance} along the normal, bevel {width, segments, profile}, subdivide, delete, flip. Vertex ops: weld (to their centre), move {offset [x,y,z]}, smooth {factor, iterations}, dissolve, bevel {width}, delete, connect (2 vertices), create_face (3-4 vertices). An op without its own select goes on with what the previous face op left selected (after extrude / inset / move / flip: the cap, the inset's inner face), like Edit Mesh; otherwise the select is read again on the mesh as it is at that op (indices too). Call with ops: [] first to preview faces / vertices (index, normal, centre). Afterwards the object counts as hand-edited (set_geometry then needs force). One undo step per call.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

select.description: which part of the mesh, in its OWN (local) space; filters AND together. mode "faces" (default) or "vertices". indices = face / vertex numbers from a preview (edit_mesh with ops: []); normal = a direction ([x,y,z] or up/down/+x/-x/+z/-z) within angle degrees (default 30); box = {min, max}; all: true

which part of the mesh, in its OWN (local) space; filters AND together. mode "faces" (default) or "vertices". indices = face / vertex numbers from a preview (edit_mesh with ops: []); normal = a direction ([x,y,z] or up/down/+x/-x/+z/-z) within angle degrees (default 30); box = {min, max}; all: true

tools.name: create_mesh
tools.title: Make a mesh from data
tools.description:
A mesh from raw data: vertices [[x, y, z], …] and faces [[i, j, k] or [i, j, k, l] …] (indices into vertices, counter-clockwise seen from outside; polygons of up to 32 corners are fanned, so keep them convex), optional uvs (one [u, v] per vertex). Up to 20000 vertices and 20000 faces; normals are computed (smooth: true for smooth shading, flatShading: true for hard facets). Colour it as you make it: materials [{color, roughness, metalness, …}] (up to 16 slots) with faceMaterials [slot per face, same order as faces] for parts in different colours; or colors [[r, g, b] 0-1, one per vertex] for a painted gradient (multiplied by the material colour). Material slots last through edit_mesh; vertex colours last only while an edit keeps the vertex count. subdivide: 1 or 2 smooths it (Catmull-Clark: a box of six quads becomes a rounded pebble, a few quads become a soft organic shape; each level about four times the faces, checked against the caps). Edit it afterwards with edit_mesh, or send new vertices with update_mesh. Returns the uuid.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

flatShading.description: true = one flat normal per triangle (low-poly look)

colors.description: one [r, g, b] (0-1) per vertex, in the order of vertices

faceMaterials.description: the materials slot of each face (0 = the first), one per face

subdivide.description: smooth the mesh 1 or 2 levels (Catmull-Clark); smooth shading follows unless smooth: false

New data for a mesh create_mesh made, by uuid, as ONE undo step: mode "replace" sends every vertex and face again (the same fields and caps as create_mesh, subdivide included); mode "patch" replaces vertices from offset on (vertices[0] lands on index offset) and keeps the faces — for moving part of a mesh made in this tab (after a reload, send "replace"). uvs/colors patch the same way. Primitives use set_geometry; to model any mesh use edit_mesh.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.description:
Make up to 50 shapes in ONE call and ONE undo step: shapes = [{action: "mesh", mesh: {…create_mesh's fields…}}, {action: "lathe", lathe: {…}}, …] with action one of lathe, tube, extrude, mesh (the same fields as create_mesh / create_lathe / extrude_shape / create_tube, parentUuid included). Every entry is checked first and nothing is made if one is wrong (the error names its index, shapes[3]); the uuids come back in the order given.

tools.name: set_material
tools.title: Change materials and textures
tools.description:
Make objects look finished: colour, roughness, metalness, emissive, opacity and texture maps, on many objects in one call. Maps take a library image hash or an https URL (https only, CORS-enabled, 16 MB, PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/AVIF; it becomes a library item first and is re-encoded like an upload; returned in assets). cc0 fetches a free CC0 material by id or name from Poly Haven (its texture names) or ambientCG (ids like "Wood051", "Bricks076", "Metal032", "Ground037"), or by words ("brown planks"); preset applies a named preset: one of Wood, Metal, Plastic, Glass, Stone, Rubber, Fish scales, Neon, or one the person saved (list_materials lists them all). faces gives just those faces their own new material slot. One undo step.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: create_shader
tools.title: Give objects a shader
tools.description:
Give objects a node shader, written as text like flow graphs: one line per node (id = type {param: value}), one per edge (source[.output] -> target.input), ending at a "surface" node. Example: c = color {value: "#ff8800"}\nout = surface\nc -> out.emissive. Call describe_shader_nodes for the types. Each object gets its own copy. Compiler errors come back in the result and nothing is written. Returns the graph key and its uniforms: a float one (u_<nodeId>_<param>) can be driven by a flow "setuniform" node on that object. scene: true makes the default for every object, which asks the host first.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: create_hud
tools.title: Add a HUD
tools.description:
Give the game a HUD (2D screen overlay): screens of elements — a timer, a score text, a health bar, buttons, an image. A screen named like an existing one gets the elements added. Returns every element id: bind live values with create_flow_nodes (a hudtext / hudbar / hudtimer node with data.element = the id, e.g. counter -> hudtext). A new screen becomes the one that shows unless active: false. One undo step.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.description:
Particles by preset name: sparkles, fire, smoke, dust, confetti, sparks, trail, wisps, fireflies, rain, snow. Without object it places a small emitter at position (rain and snow hang at cloud height over it); with object it attaches to that object (a torch, a campfire log). overrides tune any field (count, lifetime, speed, gravity, sizeStart, colorStart, colorEnd, opacity, …). remove: true takes them off. Scatter many instances over a terrain or any mesh (a forest on hills, rocks on a beach, flowers on a slope): asset = a primitive (Box, Sphere, Cone, Cylinder, Capsule, Dodecahedron) or a model id from search_assets, or assets = up to 8 mixed evenly. density per m² (or count), scale range, rules {slope: [min°, max°], height: [min, max] m, layer: {i, min}} keep them where they belong. tools.description:
Make or change a terrain. Without uuid it makes one (size metres, at position); with uuid it changes that one. Shape by noise: height (metres), detail (0.005-0.6), octaves, ridged, warp, edges (flat|island|bowl), seed. Sculpt with ops [{op: raise|lower|smooth|flatten, at: [x, z] from the terrain's centre, radius, strength 0-1, height (metres, raise/lower), passes}] and paint with {op: "paint", at, radius, layer 0-3, strength}. layers: up to 4 {color, texture (a library hash or a pattern name like grass, sand, stone), tiling}. It becomes a library image, shared with every peer.

tools.name: water
tools.title: Add or change water
tools.description:
Water: without uuid it makes a body of water — kind tank, pool, round, lake or ocean, size [w, h, d], at position (its bottom centre). With uuid it changes one (or makes an object water with a preset). preset: pool, aquarium, ocean, lake, river, lava, swamp, toxic, ice. level 0-1 (how full), color, look {shallowColor, deepColor, clarity, foam, …}, waves {count, amplitude, wavelength, speed, direction}, flow. tools.title: Place a sound
tools.description:
A sound in the world: asset = a library sound (search_assets kinds ["sound"]) or an https URL of a sound file (it is checked and added to the library first). Positional: heard near position (or on object), radius metres. Without on it loops all the time (a campfire crackle, a river); on: click | enter | exit | grab | hit plays it once when that happens on the object. One undo step for the file's node and its wiring.

tools.name: set_music
tools.title: Set the background music

The scene's background music, heard by everyone in sync: asset = a library sound or an https URL (null clears it), volume 0-1, play / stop. One undo step.

tools.name: undo_last
tools.title: Undo your last change
tools.description:
Take back your own last tool call (count for several, newest first). Use it whenever the person says "undo that" or "take that back": they may be talking and cannot see each call. Only ever undoes YOUR calls. If someone has since changed the same objects it refuses and lists them, and nothing changes: tell the person who changed what. Before a big change, save a checkpoint ({checkpoint: "before the roof"}); {restore: "before the roof"} goes back to it (up to 10 names).
When the person says "undo that" or "take that back", call undo_last; if it refuses, say who changed what.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: set_pivot
tools.title: Set the point an object turns about
tools.description:
Set the point an object turns and scales about, without moving it: a head that nods at the neck, a lamp that tilts at its joint, a door on its hinge. After this, update_objects rotation and scale, clips and Spin nodes all turn it about that point. list_scene reports it as `pivot`.

tools.name: create_pivot
tools.title: Make a pivot group
tools.description:
Make a group at a point and put objects in it, so turning the group swings them about that point: arm parts about a shoulder, several parts of a lamp about one joint. The objects stay where they are. Give the point as at (world) or local (in the group the objects are already in — the numbers list_scene shows inside it). For one object, set_pivot needs no extra group. Returns groupUuid.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: add_image
tools.title: Add an image to the library
tools.description:
Put an image into the shared library (Explorer) and get its hash, for texture slots (update_objects materialParams.map, set_material) and image nodes. Give exactly one source: `url` (https, the site must allow other origins), `data` (base64, also how to pass an image you generated), or `canvas` (draw one from shapes, gradients, checkers and noise: textures, signs, labels). It is re-encoded here, so nothing in the file survives but its pixels. Limits: 16 MB in, 4096 px on the long side (larger is scaled down), a canvas 2048 px and 500 ops. One undo step; editors and admins only.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

Ops in order: rect {x,y,w,h,radius?,fill?,stroke?,lineWidth?}, circle {x,y,r,fill?,stroke?}, line {points,closed?,stroke?,fill?,lineWidth?}, text {text,x,y,size?,font: sans|serif|mono,bold?,align?,fill?}, gradient {kind: linear|radial,angle?,stops: [[0,"#111"],[1,"#eee"]]}, checker {cols,rows,colors: [a,b]}, stripes {count,vertical?,colors: [a,b]}, noise {scale,octaves?,seed?,opacity?,colors: [dark,light]} (tiles at the edges). tools.name: inspect_runtime

tools.description: Read what the game is doing right now, without changing anything: when each event and action node last fired, the game state and variables, who runs the physics and the game rules, behaviour and script errors, and what the HUD shows. Pass node (a flow node id) or object (a uuid) to ask "why didn't it fire?": it names the missing link (no source upstream, a selector wired the wrong way, nothing clicked it yet). Action nodes run only when an upstream source fires; firing one directly does nothing.

tools.name: validate_scene
tools.title: Check the game for problems
tools.description: Check the scene for what would not work when someone presses Play: actions nothing fires, an Object Selector wired the wrong way round, a scene-graph On Click that reaches no object, Game Start wired as an event, HUD nodes pointing at elements that do not exist, walk mode with no spawn, a scene with no light, behaviour code problems. Each issue says what to fix. Run it after building a game, then playtest.

tools.name: playtest
tools.title: Play the game as a test player
tools.description:
Play the game as a virtual player in YOUR OWN Play (agent page only; it never moves a person): walk a path, look at a point, click or grab an object, press a key or a HUD button, wait. Then it reports which nodes fired, the game state before and after, what the HUD shows and any errors. It fires SOURCES the way a player does (a click reaches On Click nodes); a step on an action node does nothing. Walk points are on the floor; your eye is 1.6 m above them. Clicks and pickups count for real in the shared game, like a person playing.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: create_flow_nodes
tools.title: Add behaviour (flow) nodes
tools.description:
Add behavior (flow) nodes to a node graph — this is how objects get MOTION and interactivity: spin, bounce, patrol a path, pulse, blink, react to clicks. graph is "scene" or an object uuid (ONE graph per call). KEY RULE: a behavior node placed in an OBJECT's graph with no edges automatically drives that object — most behaviors are one node, zero edges, so usually OMIT edges. A script node runs every frame FROM THE BASE POSE, so object.rotation.y += 0.02 lands at base + 0.02 and stays: write object.rotation.y = base.rot[1] + elapsed * speed (base has pos, rot, scale as arrays; elapsed = seconds since Play started, time = the shared clock, seconds of the day, a large number). Particle gravity is the acceleration along world Y: negative falls, positive rises. Describe nodes EITHER as text (graph lines, see the system prompt) OR as nodes/edges arrays. A call with some bad nodes still creates the good ones and returns partial:true + errors[] — resend only what errors[] names.
Motion and interaction are flow nodes (create_flow_nodes); call describe_node_types before wiring edges.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

graph.description: "scene" or an existing object uuid (nodes in an object's graph drive that object)

text.description: graph lines: `ref = type "label" {params}` per new node (omitted params = defaults), `ref.out -> other.in` per wire (refs or existing node ids). e.g. "c = onclick\nl = latch {initial: false}\nc -> l.set"

ref.description: local key so edges in THIS call can reference the new node

type.description: a node type from the system prompt's Node types

data.description: node params, e.g. spin {axis:"y",speed:2}; bounce {amplitude:0.5,speed:2}; pathpatrol {points:[[x,y,z],…] (>=2 world waypoints), speed:1, mode:"loop"|"pingpong"}; setcolor {color:"#ff0000"}; latch {initial:false}; delay {seconds:3}; sequence {delay1:0,delay2:0.5,delay3:0.5,delay4:0.5} (delays are CUMULATIVE). Omit for defaults.

edges.description: optional wires between nodes (by ref or existing node id). Usually OMIT — unwired behavior nodes already drive their graph's object.

tools.name: update_flow_nodes
tools.title: Change or remove flow nodes
tools.description:
Tune or remove existing behavior nodes in one graph. Node ids and current data are in the scene summary under each object's "flow" (and "sceneFlow"). Script code runs every frame from the base pose: use object.rotation.y = base.rot[1] + elapsed * speed, not += (elapsed = seconds since Play started, time = the shared clock, seconds of the day).
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: describe_node_types
tools.title: Look up flow node types
tools.description:
Look up flow node types before wiring them: per type its inputs (toHandle names + socket types), its output type and named outputs (fromHandle), its params with types and defaults, and one line on what it does. No arguments = every type name by group; group = that group with one-line docs; types = full details (up to 12). Changes nothing.
Motion and interaction are flow nodes (create_flow_nodes); call describe_node_types before wiring edges.

tools.name: create_behaviour
tools.title: Add a code behaviour

source.description: the whole behaviour module source (plain JavaScript, the format in create_behaviour's description). Must be deterministic: no Math.random (use rand()), no Date.now/new Date (use the session clock), no DOM, no localStorage, no timers (use this.after), no loop without an exit.

tools.name: edit_behaviour
tools.title: Edit a code behaviour
tools.description:
Replace an existing behaviour's source (the scene summary lists them; read the current source with the name). Linted before it is applied. Same format as create_behaviour (see its description).
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

source.description: the whole behaviour module source (plain JavaScript, the format in create_behaviour's description). Must be deterministic: no Math.random (use rand()), no Date.now/new Date (use the session clock), no DOM, no localStorage, no timers (use this.after), no loop without an exit.

tools.name: set_physics
tools.title: Set physics
tools.description:
Set physics body params on objects (batch). NOTE: objects made with create_objects are STATIC unless created with physics "dynamic" or a mass — use this to make existing objects dynamic, to TUNE bodies, or to pin scenery (mode "static"). mode "auto" reverts to scenery defaults.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

collidesWith.description: groups this object collides with (omit = all); leave out player for a ghost wall the player walks through

tools.name: create_joints
tools.title: Add physics joints
tools.description:
Attach object pairs with physics joints: "fixed" welds them rigidly, "revolute" hinges around an axis (optional motor spins it). Move parts to their final pose WORLD-ALIGNED (no rotation) before jointing. Without anchor a hinge sits at b's origin (its centre) and a weld midway: pass anchor [x,y,z] (world) for the real pivot, e.g. the top of a pendulum rod or a door's edge. Jointed bodies that touch (a door in its frame, a wheel in its arch) also need contacts:false, or the solver pushes them apart.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

b.description: uuid of the attached object (hinge anchors at its origin)

anchor.description: world [x,y,z] of the pivot/weld point (default: b's origin for a hinge, midway for a weld)

contacts.description: false = the two bodies stop colliding with each other (default true)

limits.description: revolute only: [min, max] radians the hinge may turn

tools.name: control_simulation
tools.title: Run or stop the simulation
tools.description:
Start, stop, pause, resume or reset the physics simulation. After building a physics assembly, start the simulation so the user sees it move.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: import_model
tools.title: Import a 3D model
tools.description:
Import a self-contained GLB (binary glTF 2.0, everything embedded, ≤ 25 MB) into the scene through the app's own import pipeline (auto-optimize, LOD, budget check). Named nodes are kept as a hierarchy and returned with uuids. One undo step; syncs to every peer; provenance is recorded. Use for models built outside the app (e.g. an img2threejs rebuild exported with named pivots). Materials: standard PBR only — custom shaders do not survive glTF.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

path.description: a local .glb path on the agent's machine (the bridge reads it)

data.description: the GLB as base64 (alternative to path/url)

url.description: an http(s) URL of a .glb (the host may block other origins)

prompt.description: the request it was made for

tools.name: import_file
tools.title: Import a file
tools.description:
Bring a file made on your machine into the session: PNG / WebP images (≤ 16 MB, metadata stripped), JSON (≤ 2 MB) or a .tpanim clip. The type is read from the bytes. It lands in the Explorer (folder "Generated" unless `folder`), shared with every peer. Pass the generator's input as `spec` and it is saved beside the file as <name>.<generator>.json (e.g. knight.png + knight.pixling.json) so it can be regenerated. Face ops: extrude {distance}, inset {amount 0-1}, move {distance} along the normal, bevel {width, segments, profile}, subdivide, delete, flip. Vertex ops: weld (to their centre), move {offset [x,y,z]}, smooth {factor, iterations}, dissolve, bevel {width}, delete, connect (2 vertices), create_face (3-4 vertices). An op without its own select goes on with what the previous face op left selected (after extrude / inset / move / flip: the cap, the inset's inner face), like Edit Mesh; otherwise the select is read again on the mesh as it is at that op (indices too). Call with ops: [] first to preview faces / vertices (index, normal, centre). Afterwards the object counts as hand-edited (edit_shape {action: 'params'} then needs force). One undo step per call.

offset.description: patch: the first vertex index the new vertices replace

update.description: New data for a mesh create_shape {action: 'mesh'} made, by uuid, as ONE undo step: mode "replace" sends every vertex and face again (the same fields and caps as create_shape {action: 'mesh'}, subdivide included); mode "patch" replaces vertices from offset on (vertices[0] lands on index offset) and keeps the faces — for moving part of a mesh made in this tab (after a reload, send "replace"). uvs/colors patch the same way. Primitives use edit_shape {action: 'params'}; to model any mesh use edit_shape {action: 'mesh'}.

preset.description: bottom = on its footprint, center = its box, median = its vertices, world = the scene origin, children = the middle of a group

reset.description: true = back to the object's own centre

pivot.description: Set the point an object turns and scales about, without moving it: a head that nods at the neck, a lamp that tilts at its joint, a door on its hinge. After this, update_objects rotation and scale, clips and Spin nodes all turn it about that point. list_scene reports it as `pivot`.

at.description: the point: [x,y,z] world metres, or "center" / "bottom" / "top" of the objects together

local.description: instead of at: [x,y,z] in the space of the group the objects are in (world space at the scene root)

pivot_group.description: Make a group at a point and put objects in it, so turning the group swings them about that point: arm parts about a shoulder, several parts of a lamp about one joint. The objects stay where they are. Give the point as at (world) or local (in the group the objects are already in — the numbers list_scene shows inside it). For one object, edit_shape {action: 'pivot'} needs no extra group. Returns groupUuid.

tools.name: set_look
tools.title: Materials, shaders, sky, light and post effects
tools.description:
How things look: material = colour, roughness, metal, glow, see-through and textures (a library image, a CC0 material by name or an https image); list_materials / get_material read them; shader / edit_shader / assign_shader / shader_nodes = node shaders on objects; sky = the sky image, background, fog and exposure; light = the sun, ambient and environment lights; environment reads both; post / get_post / post_graph = the scene's post effects (bloom, colour grade, vignette); sky, light and post change the whole scene, so the host is asked first; unwrap / uv = texture mapping and tiling.
Call it as {"action": "material", "material": {…its fields…}}; each action's fields and limits are in its object below.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

action.description: What to do. Put its fields in the object named after the action.

color.description: base colour: hex or a CSS name

emissive.description: glow colour: hex or a CSS name

params.description: any other material number, e.g. {"clearcoat": 1, "transmission": 0.9, "ior": 1.5} (those need type MeshPhysicalMaterial)

pattern.description: 85b: a procedural albedo texture by name — wood, planks, brick, tiles, marble, stone, concrete, metal, grass, sand, fabric, checker, stripes, noise — or {name, colors: [dark, light], scale, seed, size}; it becomes a library image first

patternScale.description: with pattern: how many times it repeats across each face (e.g. 4 for a floor)

maps.description: texture slots, each a library image hash, an https URL, {pattern: name} (a procedural texture), or null to clear

preset.description: a preset: Wood, Metal, Plastic, Glass, Stone, Rubber, Fish scales, Neon, or a saved one list_materials names

cc0.description: a CC0 material by Poly Haven name, ambientCG id ("Wood051", "Bricks076", "Metal032") or words ("brown planks")

slot.description: which material slot of a multi-material object (default 0)

faces.description: which faces: {"normal": "up"|"down"|"+x"|"-x"|"+z"|"-z"|[x,y,z], "angle": 30}, {"box": {"min": [..], "max": [..]}} (local space), {"indices": [..]} or {"all": true}; filters AND together

material.description: Make objects look finished: colour, roughness, metalness, emissive, opacity and texture maps, on many objects in one call. Maps take a library image hash or an https URL (https only, CORS-enabled, 16 MB, PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/AVIF; it becomes a library item first and is re-encoded like an upload; returned in assets). cc0 fetches a free CC0 material by id or name from Poly Haven (its texture names) or ambientCG (ids like "Wood051", "Bricks076", "Metal032", "Ground037"), or by words ("brown planks"); preset applies a named preset: one of Wood, Metal, Plastic, Glass, Stone, Rubber, Fish scales, Neon, or one the person saved (set_look {action: 'list_materials'} lists them all). faces gives just those faces their own new material slot. One undo step.

name.description: only objects whose name contains this

list_materials.description: What objects wear: per object its material slots (type, colour, numbers, which maps) and shader, plus the preset names (the starters Wood, Metal, Plastic, Glass, Stone, Rubber, Fish scales, Neon, and any the person saved) and shader keys. Read this before editing.

get_material.description: One object's material in full: every slot, each map's tiling / offset / rotation / size / hash, and its shader graph as text with the uniforms a flow can drive.

replace.description: replace a graph the object already has

scene.description: the scene default instead of objects (asks the host)

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

shader.description: Give objects a node shader, written as text like flow graphs: one line per node (id = type {param: value}), one per edge (source[.output] -> target.input), ending at a "surface" node. Example: c = color {value: "#ff8800"}\nout = surface\nc -> out.emissive. Call set_look {action: 'shader_nodes'} for the types. Each object gets its own copy. Compiler errors come back in the result and nothing is written. Returns the graph key and its uniforms: a float one (u_<nodeId>_<param>) can be driven by a flow "setuniform" node on that object. scene: true makes the default for every object, which asks the host first.
the key from create_shader or list_materials

add.description: text: nodes to add or replace and edges to add

edit_shader.description: Change a shader graph: params [{node, param, value}] for values, add (text: new or replaced nodes, new edges), removeNodes, or text for the whole graph. Errors come back and nothing changes.

shader.description: the key of the graph to copy, or null to remove

assign_shader.description: Copy an existing shader graph onto objects (each gets its own copy), or take a shader off with shader: null.

shader_nodes.description: The shader node catalog: each type with what it does, its params (which become uniforms), inputs and outputs.

enabled.description: the whole stack on or off

camera.description: a camera's own look instead of the scene's

mode.description: camera look: add to the scene look, or replace it

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

post.description: The scene's post effects (bloom, huesaturation, brightnesscontrast, tonemapping, vignette, grain, chromaticaberration, ao, lut, pixelation, scanlines, dotscreen, smaa; set_look {action: 'get_post'} lists every param). effects: [{kind, params, enabled, at, remove}], matched to what is there by id or kind, so repeating a call does not stack a second bloom; replace: true drops the rest; the stack order is the order of effect. This changes the whole scene's look: the first call returns needsConfirm and the host is asked; repeat it with confirmId. One undo step.

camera.description: a camera's own look instead of the scene's

get_post.description: The look stack as it is (effects with ids and params) and every effect kind with its params and ranges.

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

post_graph.description: A custom post effect: a preset, or a shader graph as text ending at a "postOutput" node (set_look {action: 'shader_nodes'} domain post), added to the look. Changes the whole scene's look, so it asks the host first like set_look {action: 'post'}. Compiler errors come back in the result.

faces.description: which faces: {"normal": "up"|"down"|"+x"|"-x"|"+z"|"-z"|[x,y,z], "angle": 30}, {"box": {"min": [..], "max": [..]}} (local space), {"indices": [..]} or {"all": true}; filters AND together

unwrap.description: New texture coordinates: smart (flat islands by surface direction, the default), box, planar, cylindrical, spherical. faces limits it to those faces and leaves the rest. Use it when a texture smears on a model. One undo step.

rotation.description: radians, about the middle of the image

faces.description: which faces: {"normal": "up"|"down"|"+x"|"-x"|"+z"|"-z"|[x,y,z], "angle": 30}, {"box": {"min": [..], "max": [..]}} (local space), {"indices": [..]} or {"all": true}; filters AND together

uv.description: Tile, shift or rotate a material slot's textures (tiling: 4 repeats a floor texture four times). maps limits it to some slots. With faces it maps only those faces instead: they are projected flat so the image fills them once (a label on one side of a box), with tiling / offset / rotation on top; pair it with set_look {action: 'material'} faces for an image only on that face. One undo step.

preset.description: studio, daylight, sunset, night, classic, clearsky, meadow, sunrise, starlight, photostudio

hdri.description: a sky name (clearsky, meadow, sunrise, starlight, photostudio), null for none, or {name | hash, rotation (degrees), intensity 0-4, blur 0-1, background (false = light only), quality, minQuality}

background.description: a colour: hex or a CSS name

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

sky.description: The sky and the air: a look preset (studio, daylight, sunset, night, classic, clearsky, meadow, sunrise, starlight, photostudio), a sky image by name (clearsky, meadow, sunrise, starlight, photostudio; or {hash} of an HDR in the library — never a URL) with rotation, intensity, blur and Sky quality (auto / standard / high / max, plus a minimum), a background colour or {top, bottom} gradient, fog ({color, near, far} in metres, or {color, density}; null = none) and exposure. "Make it night": preset night or hdri starlight + a dark fog. Changes the whole scene's look, so the host is asked first: it answers needsConfirm, then repeat with confirmId. One undo step.

confirmId.description: the id a needsConfirm answer gave: repeat the call with it to get the host's answer and apply

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the answer (up to 60)

light.description: The scene's own lighting: sun {color, intensity, direction [x,y,z] the light shines (y below 0)} or null for none, ambient {sky, ground, intensity} or null, and environment lights (directional / point / hemisphere, at most 8): add [{kind, color, intensity, position}], update [{id, …}], remove [ids] (set_look {action: 'environment'} lists their ids). Lamps, spots and area lights in the scene are objects: create_objects kind light. Changes the whole scene's look, so the host is asked first (needsConfirm, then repeat with confirmId). One undo step.

names.description: false = leave out the preset and sky name lists

environment.description: Read the scene's sky and light: the preset, the sky image and its quality, background, fog, exposure, the sun and ambient, the environment lights (ids for set_look {action: 'light'}), the light objects (uuid, shadows) and the spawn / opening view; plus the preset and sky names. Read this before changing the look.

tools.name: run
tools.title: See and check what the game does
tools.description:
What the game does when it runs: inspect = when each event and action last fired, the game state and variables, errors, and why a node did not fire (pass node or object); validate = what would not work when someone presses Play, each with its fix; logs = the tab's recent errors, warnings and toasts.
Call it as {"action": "inspect", "inspect": {…its fields…}}; each action's fields and limits are in its object below.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

action.description: What to do. Put its fields in the object named after the action.

node.description: a flow node id: explain this node

object.description: an object uuid: its nodes and why they did or did not fire

inspect.description: Read what the game is doing right now, without changing anything: when each event and action node last fired, the game state and variables, who runs the physics and the game rules, behaviour and script errors, and what the HUD shows. Pass node (a flow node id) or object (a uuid) to ask "why didn't it fire?": it names the missing link (no source upstream, a selector wired the wrong way, nothing clicked it yet). Action nodes run only when an upstream source fires; firing one directly does nothing.

validate.description: Check the scene for what would not work when someone presses Play: actions nothing fires, an Object Selector wired the wrong way round, a scene-graph On Click that reaches no object, Game Start wired as an event, HUD nodes pointing at elements that do not exist, walk mode with no spawn, a scene with no light, behaviour code problems. Each issue says what to fix. Run it after building a game, then playtest.

since.description: only lines after this time (ms since 1970, the "now" a previous logs answer gave)

level.description: the lowest level to include (default info)

logs.description: The page's recent log: errors, warnings, console lines and the toasts people saw, oldest first. Pass since (the "now" of the previous answer) for only what is new. status shows the newest few.

annotations.title: See and check what the game does

tools.name: assets
tools.title: Images and assets
tools.description:
Assets to build with: search = find models, prefabs, sounds, images, CC0 materials and HDRIs by words (library, packs, Poly Haven); place = put a found model or prefab into the scene; prefab = keep objects as a reusable prefab, or place copies of one; image = put an image into the library (an https URL, base64 data, or a canvas you describe) and get its hash for textures.
Call it as {"action": "search", "search": {…its fields…}}; each action's fields and limits are in its object below.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

action.description: What to do. Put its fields in the object named after the action.

query.description: words, e.g. "pine tree", "wooden crate", "campfire crackle"; empty lists everything of the kinds

search.description: Find assets to build with, by words and kind: models and prefabs to place, sounds, images, CC0 materials and HDRIs. Searches the shared library, the model packs, your prefabs and Poly Haven. Each result has an id, name, kind, source, licence, size when known, and how to use it. Read-only.

asset.description: an id from search_assets: lib:<hash>, pack:<pack>/<item> or prefab:<id>

position.description: world metres; the model stands on this point

place.description: Place a model or assets {action: 'prefab'} found with assets {action: 'search'}, the way dragging it from the Asset Browser does (replicated, one undo step). count + spacing make a row; yaw turns it. Returns the new uuids. A model by URL goes through import_model instead.

objects.description: save: the uuids to keep together

prefab.description: place: the prefab id (prefab:…) or its name

Prefabs (stamps): mode "save" keeps objects (with their materials, flows and behaviours) as a assets {action: 'prefab'} in this person's library and returns its id; mode "place" puts copies of a assets {action: 'prefab'} into the scene with fresh ids (count + spacing for a row), one undo step.

url.description: https address of a PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or AVIF

data.description: the image as base64, or this part of it

chunk.description: a large image in parts: every part has the same id; it is added when the last part arrives

canvas.description: Draw an image from data. Coordinates in pixels from the top left. Ops in order: rect {x,y,w,h,radius?,fill?,stroke?,lineWidth?}, circle {x,y,r,fill?,stroke?}, line {points,closed?,stroke?,fill?,lineWidth?}, text {text,x,y,size?,font: sans|serif|mono,bold?,align?,fill?}, gradient {kind: linear|radial,angle?,stops: [[0,"#111"],[1,"#eee"]]}, checker {cols,rows,colors: [a,b]}, stripes {count,vertical?,colors: [a,b]}, noise {scale,octaves?,seed?,opacity?,colors: [dark,light]} (tiles at the edges). Colours: hex or a CSS name.

name.description: the file name in the library

prompt.description: a generated image: the request it was made for

source.description: where it came from, e.g. the generator

place.description: also place it in the scene as a card (default false)

image.description: Put an image into the shared library (Explorer) and get its hash, for texture slots (update_objects materialParams.map, set_look {action: 'material'}) and image nodes. Give exactly one source: `url` (https, the site must allow other origins), `data` (base64, also how to pass an image you generated), or `canvas` (draw one from shapes, gradients, checkers and noise: textures, signs, labels). It is re-encoded here, so nothing in the file survives but its pixels. Limits: 16 MB in, 4096 px on the long side (larger is scaled down), a canvas 2048 px and 500 ops. One undo step; editors and admins only.

tools.name: effects
tools.title: Terrain, scatter, water, particles and sound
tools.description:
The world around the build: terrain = make or shape ground (noise hills, sculpt, paint layers); scatter = many trees, rocks or flowers over a terrain or mesh, with slope / height rules; water = a pool, lake or ocean, or make an object water; particles = fire, smoke, sparkles, fireflies, rain, snow … by preset; sound = a positional sound (looping, or on click / enter); music = the scene's background track.
Call it as {"action": "terrain", "terrain": {…its fields…}}; each action's fields and limits are in its object below.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

action.description: What to do. Put its fields in the object named after the action.

pattern.description: a procedural texture by name — wood (wood grain), planks (wooden planks with seams), brick (red brick in running bond), tiles (square tiles with grout), marble (white marble with veins), stone (cobbles / round stones), concrete (grey concrete), metal (brushed metal), grass (grass), sand (sand), fabric (woven fabric), checker (a checkerboard), stripes (stripes), noise (soft noise) — or {name, colors: [dark, light, …], scale: repeats of the motif (1 = its own), seed, size: 128|256|512|1024}. It becomes a library image, shared with every peer.

force.description: reshape even though it was hand-sculpted (the sculpting is lost)

terrain.description: Make or change a effects {action: 'terrain'}. Without uuid it makes one (size metres, at position); with uuid it changes that one. Shape by noise: height (metres), detail (0.005-0.6), octaves, ridged, warp, edges (flat|island|bowl), seed. Sculpt with ops [{op: raise|lower|smooth|flatten, at: [x, z] from the effects {action: 'terrain'}'s centre, radius, strength 0-1, height (metres, raise/lower), passes}] and paint with {op: "paint", at, radius, layer 0-3, strength}. layers: up to 4 {color, texture (a library hash or a pattern name like grass, sand, stone), tiling}. One undo step.

scale.description: [min, max] size factors (default [0.8, 1.2]) or one number

rules.description: {slope: [0, 25] degrees from flat, height: [min, max] metres, layer: {i: paint layer 0-3, min: 0-1}}

remove.description: a set id to delete instead

scatter.description: Scatter many instances over a effects {action: 'terrain'} or any mesh (a forest on hills, rocks on a beach, flowers on a slope): asset = a primitive (Box, Sphere, Cone, Cylinder, Capsule, Dodecahedron) or a model id from assets {action: 'search'}, or assets = up to 8 mixed evenly. density per m² (or count), scale range, rules {slope: [min°, max°], height: [min, max] m, layer: {i, min}} keep them where they belong. Cheap instancing, seeded (the same on every peer). Returns the set id; remove: <set id> deletes a set. One undo step.

water.description: Water: without uuid it makes a body of effects {action: 'water'} — kind tank, pool, round, lake or ocean, size [w, h, d], at position (its bottom centre). With uuid it changes one (or makes an object effects {action: 'water'} with a preset). preset: pool, aquarium, ocean, lake, river, lava, swamp, toxic, ice. level 0-1 (how full), color, look {shallowColor, deepColor, clarity, foam, …}, waves {count, amplitude, wavelength, speed, direction}, flow. Things float in it in Play. remove: true makes it a plain object again. One undo step.

object.description: attach to this object (uuid) instead of placing an emitter

overrides.description: particle fields: mode, count, lifetime, lifeJitter, shape, angle, radius, offset, speed, speedJitter, gravity, drag, turbulence, sizeStart, sizeEnd, colorStart, colorEnd, colorMode, opacity, fadeIn, fadeOut, sprite, blending, spin, space, aim, render, inherit, stretch, trail, trailSegments

particles.description: Particles by preset name: sparkles, fire, smoke, dust, confetti, sparks, trail, wisps, fireflies, rain, snow. Without object it places a small emitter at position (rain and snow hang at cloud height over it); with object it attaches to that object (a torch, a campfire log). overrides tune any field (count, lifetime, speed, gravity, sizeStart, colorStart, colorEnd, opacity, …). remove: true takes them off. One undo step.

asset.description: lib:<hash>, a library hash, or https://…

object.description: put the sound on this object (uuid) instead of at position

sound.description: A sound in the world: asset = a library sound (assets {action: 'search'} kinds ["sound"]) or an https URL of a sound file (it is checked and added to the library first). Positional: heard near position (or on object), radius metres. Without on it loops all the time (a campfire crackle, a river); on: click | enter | exit | grab | hit plays it once when that happens on the object. One undo step for the file's node and its wiring.

music.description: The scene's background music, heard by everyone in sync: asset = a library sound or an https URL (null clears it), volume 0-1, play / stop. One undo step.

tools.name: game_setup
tools.title: Game setup: spawn and play camera
tools.description:
How the game starts: spawn = where Play starts and which way the player faces; play_camera = first person walking or flying (speed, jump, eye height) and openingView = where the editor camera starts when the scene opens.
Call it as {"action": "spawn", "spawn": {…its fields…}}; each action's fields and limits are in its object below.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

action.description: What to do. Put its fields in the object named after the action.

spawn.description: Where Play starts: position [x, y, z] of the player's feet (or object: a uuid to stand on top of), facing a point [x, y, z] or an object uuid (or yaw in radians, 0 faces -Z); clear: true removes it. One undo step.

tools.name: undo_last
tools.title: Undo your last change
tools.description:
Take back your own last tool call (count for several, newest first). Use it whenever the person says "undo that" or "take that back": they may be talking and cannot see each call. Only ever undoes YOUR calls. If someone has since changed the same objects it refuses and lists them, and nothing changes: tell the person who changed what. Before a big change, save a checkpoint ({checkpoint: "before the roof"}); {restore: "before the roof"} goes back to it (up to 10 names).
When the person says "undo that" or "take that back", call undo_last; if it refuses, say who changed what.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

checkpoint.description: save this moment under a name ("before the roof") to come back to; nothing is undone

wait.description: with confirmId: seconds to wait for the host's answer (at most 60)

tools.name: playtest
tools.title: Play the game as a test player
tools.description:
Play the game as a virtual player in YOUR OWN Play (agent page only; it never moves a person): walk a path, look at a point, click or grab an object, press a key or a HUD button, wait. Then it reports which nodes fired, the game state before and after, what the HUD shows and any errors. It fires SOURCES the way a player does (a click reaches On Click nodes); a step on an action node does nothing. Walk points are on the floor; your eye is 1.6 m above them. Clicks and pickups count for real in the shared game, like a person playing.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

steps.description: in order, each ONE of: {walk: [[x,y,z], …], speed?} · {look: [x,y,z]} · {click: uuid} · {grab: uuid} · {key: "KeyE", hold?} · {hud: elementId} · {wait: seconds}

stayInPlay.description: keep this page in Play afterwards (default: leave Play if the playtest entered it)

tools.name: create_flow_nodes
tools.title: Add behaviour (flow) nodes
tools.description:
Add behavior (flow) nodes to a node graph — this is how objects get MOTION and interactivity: spin, bounce, patrol a path, pulse, blink, react to clicks. graph is "scene" or an object uuid (ONE graph per call). KEY RULE: a behavior node placed in an OBJECT's graph with no edges automatically drives that object — most behaviors are one node, zero edges, so usually OMIT edges. A script node runs every frame FROM THE BASE POSE, so object.rotation.y += 0.02 lands at base + 0.02 and stays: write object.rotation.y = base.rot[1] + elapsed * speed (base has pos, rot, scale as arrays; elapsed = seconds since Play started, time = the shared clock, seconds of the day, a large number). Particle gravity is the acceleration along world Y: negative falls, positive rises. Describe nodes EITHER as text (graph lines, see the system prompt) OR as nodes/edges arrays. A call with some bad nodes still creates the good ones and returns partial:true + errors[] — resend only what errors[] names.
Motion and interaction are flow nodes (create_flow_nodes); call describe_node_types before wiring edges.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

graph.description: "scene" or an existing object uuid (nodes in an object's graph drive that object)

text.description: graph lines: `ref = type "label" {params}` per new node (omitted params = defaults), `ref.out -> other.in` per wire (refs or existing node ids). e.g. "c = onclick\nl = latch {initial: false}\nc -> l.set"

ref.description: local key so edges in THIS call can reference the new node

type.description: a node type from the system prompt's Node types

data.description: node params, e.g. spin {axis:"y",speed:2}; bounce {amplitude:0.5,speed:2}; pathpatrol {points:[[x,y,z],…] (>=2 world waypoints), speed:1, mode:"loop"|"pingpong"}; setcolor {color:"#ff0000"}; latch {initial:false}; delay {seconds:3}; sequence {delay1:0,delay2:0.5,delay3:0.5,delay4:0.5} (delays are CUMULATIVE). Omit for defaults.

edges.description: optional wires between nodes (by ref or existing node id). Usually OMIT — unwired behavior nodes already drive their graph's object.

tools.name: update_flow_nodes
tools.title: Change or remove flow nodes
tools.description:
Tune or remove existing behavior nodes in one graph. Node ids and current data are in the scene summary under each object's "flow" (and "sceneFlow"). Script code runs every frame from the base pose: use object.rotation.y = base.rot[1] + elapsed * speed, not += (elapsed = seconds since Play started, time = the shared clock, seconds of the day).
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

tools.name: describe_node_types
tools.title: Look up flow node types
tools.description:
Look up flow node types before wiring them: per type its inputs (toHandle names + socket types), its output type and named outputs (fromHandle), its params with types and defaults, and one line on what it does. No arguments = every type name by group; group = that group with one-line docs; types = full details (up to 12). Changes nothing.
Motion and interaction are flow nodes (create_flow_nodes); call describe_node_types before wiring edges.

tools.name: set_physics
tools.title: Set physics
tools.description:
Set physics body params on objects (batch). NOTE: objects made with create_objects are STATIC unless created with physics "dynamic" or a mass — use this to make existing objects dynamic, to TUNE bodies, or to pin scenery (mode "static"). mode "auto" reverts to scenery defaults.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

collider.description: trimesh = the exact mesh, for static scenery (tunnels, pools, arches); a dynamic body gets its hull

sensor.description: true = a trigger volume: no collision response, fires On Enter/On Exit nodes

group.description: collision group; water = a pass-through trigger volume

collidesWith.description: groups this object collides with (omit = all); leave out player for a ghost wall the player walks through

tools.name: create_joints
tools.title: Add physics joints
tools.description:
Attach object pairs with physics joints: "fixed" welds them rigidly, "revolute" hinges around an axis (optional motor spins it). Move parts to their final pose WORLD-ALIGNED (no rotation) before jointing. Without anchor a hinge sits at b's origin (its centre) and a weld midway: pass anchor [x,y,z] (world) for the real pivot, e.g. the top of a pendulum rod or a door's edge. Jointed bodies that touch (a door in its frame, a wheel in its arch) also need contacts:false, or the solver pushes them apart.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

b.description: uuid of the attached object (hinge anchors at its origin)

anchor.description: world [x,y,z] of the pivot/weld point (default: b's origin for a hinge, midway for a weld)

contacts.description: false = the two bodies stop colliding with each other (default true)

limits.description: revolute only: [min, max] radians the hinge may turn

tools.name: control_simulation
tools.title: Run or stop the simulation
tools.description:
Start, stop, pause, resume or reset the physics simulation. After building a physics assembly, start the simulation so the user sees it move.

tools.name: import_model
tools.title: Import a 3D model
tools.description:
Import a self-contained GLB (binary glTF 2.0, everything embedded, ≤ 25 MB) into the scene through the app's own import pipeline (auto-optimize, LOD, budget check). Named nodes are kept as a hierarchy and returned with uuids. One undo step; syncs to every peer; provenance is recorded. Use for models built outside the app (e.g. an img2threejs rebuild exported with named pivots). Materials: standard PBR only — custom shaders do not survive glTF.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

path.description: a local .glb path on the agent's machine (the bridge reads it)

data.description: the GLB as base64 (alternative to path/url)

url.description: an http(s) URL of a .glb (the host may block other origins)

parent.description: uuid (or exact name) of the object to parent under

source.description: where the model came from, e.g. "img2threejs from photo campfire.jpg"

licence.description: its licence, e.g. CC0, CC-BY-4.0, "own work"

prompt.description: the request it was made for

tools.name: import_file
tools.title: Import a file
tools.description:
Bring a file made on your machine into the session: PNG / WebP images (≤ 16 MB, metadata stripped), JSON (≤ 2 MB) or a .tpanim clip. The type is read from the bytes. It lands in the Explorer (folder "Generated" unless `folder`), shared with every peer. Pass the generator's input as `spec` and it is saved beside the file as <name>.<generator>.json (e.g. knight.png + knight.pixling.json) so it can be regenerated. An image is also placed in the scene as a card (a plane; `place: false` to skip): `filter: "nearest"` keeps pixel art crisp (default when a spec is given), `frame: {w, h, col, row}` shows one frame of a sprite sheet, `facing: "camera-y"` turns it to face each viewer. One undo step; editors and admins only. Large files: send base64 parts with `chunk: {id, index, total}` (the bridge does this for you with `path`).
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

path.description: a local file on the agent's machine (the bridge reads it)

data.description: the file as base64 (or this chunk's part of it)

chunk.description: a chunked upload: every part has the same id; the import runs when the last part arrives

name.description: the file name in the Explorer (its extension comes from the bytes)

spec.description: the generator input (JSON object or string), saved beside the file

spec_path.description: the spec as a local .json file (the bridge reads it)

place.description: images: place a card in the scene (default true)

position.description: [x,y,z] metres (default: standing on the ground at the origin)

height.description: card height in metres (default 1; width follows the aspect)

width.description: card width in metres (instead of height)

frame.description: show one frame of a sheet: w/h in pixels, col/row from 0 (row 0 = top)

filter.description: texture filtering (auto = nearest for pixel art)

facing.description: billboard: face each viewer (camera-y = turn about Y only)

lit.description: shade the card with the scene lights (default unlit, like a sprite)

source.description: where it came from, e.g. "pixling 0.3.1 build specs/knight.json"

tools.name: connect
tools.title: Join a session
tools.description:
Join a theprototype.app session. Pass the link the host shared (https://theprototype.app/#F0FD3, possibly with &invite=…) or the bare session id. An invite link joins at once; a plain link asks the host to Approve. The scene tools appear once the agent page is up; call status to see whether you are in.

tools.name: status
tools.title: Session status
tools.description:
Where the agent is: connection state, whether the host has let it in, its role (viewer edits stay local), the app version, and why any tool is missing. sceneBudget says how heavy the scene is: objects, triangles (per frame drawn; the scene's own count while the view is idle, then no draw calls), draw calls, textures, lights you placed, frame time p95, tier green / amber / red on the desktop or vr profile, and over = each budget past green (build lighter, or stop adding, while it is not green).
You are building in the person's own open theprototype.app tab: a live, shared 3D scene. Every change shows for everyone in the session and can be undone.
This may be a VOICE conversation: answer in one or two short spoken sentences and say what changed in plain words ("Added three trees by the fire"). Never read out uuids, lists of numbers or JSON.
If a tool says the tab is closed or not connected, tell the person to open theprototype.app and press Connect Claude, then wait; do not retry in a loop.
Call status first: it says whether you may edit (a viewer can only look).
You act as this person in their own tab: status "you" is them (their peer id, name and role); the other users are everyone else.

Answers with the camera it used.

tools.name: join_session
tools.title: Join a session (asks the person)
tools.description:
Join a theprototype.app session from a link the person gave you (https://theprototype.app/#F0FD3, possibly with &invite=…, or the bare session id). Nothing happens until the person presses Join on a card in their tab that names the host and the session; Cancel refuses. The app may then ask them what to do with the scene they have open. Answers joining, refused or cancelled; call status afterwards to see where the tab is.
Take a screenshot after each change to check your work.

link.description: the session link, invite link or session id the person gave you

tools.name: where_are_users
tools.title: Where the people are
tools.description:
Where each person in the session is and which way they look (their desktop camera, or the VR headset): position, facing as a compass yaw plus forward and right vectors, the floor under them, and ready-made spots 1.5 m and 3 m in front of them at floor level. The entry with "you": true is the person you act as. Use it for "in front of me", "around me", "behind me", "to my left". A person can PING a spot (Ctrl+Alt+click, Ping in a menu, the VR stick click): each row carries their latestPing, and pings: true lists the recent ones (2 minutes). For "put it here", build with create_objects / update_objects at: {ping: "latest"} (align: "surface" for a wall). Each row also has body (eye, height, shoulder, hip, knee, reach, room — "a table at hip height") and, in VR, hands (left, right, apart — "as wide as my hands"). Nothing you make may appear inside a person in VR (0.45 m around the head, through the body): that call is refused and says so.
You act as this person in their own tab: status "you" is them (their peer id, name and role); the other users are everyone else.
For "in front of me", call where_are_users and build at the spots it gives, facing the person (face_user: true). For "here" or "this", build at the person's latest ping: at: {ping: "latest"}; ask them to ping (Ctrl+Alt+click, or Ping in the menu) if they have none.

pings.description: also list the recent pings (85b S2): id, who, how long ago, position, surface normal, the object it is on
